agency_name: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS)
mission: In collaboration with our partners, the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services provides essential services to improve the health, safety, and well-being of all North Carolinians.
user: The NCDHHS federal-grants coordinator who reviews new Grants.gov postings each week, decides which are worth pursuing, and routes each one to the division that would own the application.

strategic_priorities.name: Health Access
strategic_priorities.description: Advance health access by increasing opportunity and outcomes for people who face greater health and situational challenges.

objectives.text: Build a culture and structure for increasing health access and reducing health disparities across the Department.
Use data, metrics and dashboards to track health disparities and outcomes and make benefits easier to apply for.
Mitigate barriers to health services: telehealth and broadband, language access, culturally competent communication, rural and underserved primary care.
Invest in partner capacity: community health workers, community-based organizations, justice-involved people's health access, Medicaid expansion enrollment.

strategic_priorities.name: Child and Family Well-Being
strategic_priorities.description: Promote child and family well-being by making it easier for children and families to access the healthcare, programs, and supports they need.

objectives.text: Meet the behavioral and mental health needs of children and families (youth mental health first aid, school health records, NC-PAL, specialty care for children with complex needs).
Reform child welfare and social services to improve safety, permanency and well-being (foster care, child welfare information systems, county support).
Increase food security for children and families (WIC, FNS/SNAP enrollment, NCCARE360 referrals, breastfeeding support, Healthy Opportunities pilots).
Improve women's health and birth outcomes (prenatal care, maternal and newborn levels of care, doulas, reproductive life planning, infant mortality).

strategic_priorities.name: Behavioral Health and Resilience
strategic_priorities.description: Support behavioral health and resilience through coordinated systems of care that make mental health and substance use services easy to access and reduce stigma.

objectives.text: Integrate behavioral and physical health care (Collaborative Care, certified community behavioral health clinics, Tailored Care Management).
Expand behavioral health supports for people involved in the justice system (capacity restoration, diversion, re-entry).
Increase access to crisis services (988, suicide prevention, statewide behavioral health referral network).
Turn the tide on the opioid and substance use crisis (evidence-based treatment, harm reduction, drug checking, collegiate recovery).
Improve behavioral health data infrastructure (behavioral health holds data, syndromic surveillance, electronic health records in state psychiatric hospitals).

strategic_priorities.name: Strong and Inclusive Workforce
strategic_priorities.description: Build a strong and inclusive workforce that supports early learning, health, and wellness across North Carolina.

objectives.text: Invest in the caregiving and direct care workforce serving older adults and people with disabilities.
Invest in the early childhood workforce (teacher credentialing, educator compensation).
Make NCDHHS an equitable workplace (recruitment, training, retention of Department staff).
Support the public health and child welfare workforce at state and local levels.

strategic_priorities.name: Operational Excellence
strategic_priorities.description: Achieve operational excellence by enabling efficient, effective, and innovative processes and services.

objectives.text: Foster data-driven decision-making (data infrastructure, integration, dashboards, staff data skills).
Be effective stewards of state resources (tracking federal funding and block grants, contracting, websites, energy, invoicing).
Work across departments through shared processes and collaboration.

layer1._comment: Objective thresholds for Layer 1 (src/deterministic.py). Nothing here is semantic. deadline_score_points are [days_until_close, score 0-10] anchors, linearly interpolated; past the last anchor the score stays at its value. financial_value_score is log-scaled between the two USD anchors; total_only_cap limits grants where only total program funding (not a per-award figure) is known.

layer2_routing._comment: Probability cutoffs on Jev's per-option probabilities. A grant is deprioritized only when Jev is confident it is irrelevant or not ours; everything else goes to Layer 3. Defaults are deliberately conservative (recall over precision) and must be re-tuned on the labeled validation sample.

layer3._comment: null = deep-analyze every grant Layer 2 routes to deep review. Set an integer to cap cost; overflow is logged, never silently dropped.

layer4_scoring._comment: Deterministic final ranking. Weights sum to 1.0. Forecasts omit deadline and re-normalize without penalty. Open grants with a missing deadline re-normalize, then receive a small uncertainty penalty on the 100-point final scale. Rolling ('accepted anytime') grants get a smaller penalty than a truly unknown deadline; rolling grants whose funds can run out (first come, first served) get none.
